Subject: Quick recap & next steps — cost sensitivity and program ask

Hi Ari — great to meet this morning. Quick write-up to capture what we discussed and the asks so nothing falls through the cracks.

Recap (from your side):
- Initial product pilot: ~30M tokens/month in month 1 (inference + reranking), expected to ramp to ~120M tokens/month by month 6 as feature usage expands.
- Target unit economics: you flagged comfort around ~$300–$400 per 1M tokens for early production.
- Monthly budget window for a seeded paid rollout: ~$40k–$60k/mo initially; finance wants clarity on committed vs consumption pricing.

Asks you made during call:
1) Eligibility for the startup program/founder credit and what that would net on the first 3 months.
2) Example committed-use scenarios (3mo, 12mo) and the incremental $/1M at each tier.
3) Any multi-year incentive or rebate structure that could bring sustained $/1M below $300 as you scale.

Attached: a simple token profile we sketched — will iterate with the numbers you shared.

Next steps (agreed):
- I’ll pull together a proposal with a few committed-use bands and a startup credit option by EOD tomorrow.
- You’ll share any final internal constraints from finance (e.g., do they need a purchase order or legal redline before we surface committed pricing).

If there’s anything missing, shout.

— Chloe Martin

chloe@redwood.ai | (650) 555-0123

Thanks Chloe — that’s a faithful recap. Two quick clarifications:
- The 30M month-1 figure includes a 10% buffer for experimentation; core steady-state month-1 load we expect ~27M.
- Budget constraint: finance will approve up to $50k/mo without additional approvals. Anything above that needs a procurement ticket and a cost justification.

On the startup credit: we’re an early seed company (raised a small round last quarter) so any founder month or pilot discount will help accelerate the POC. If you can show a net-first-3-months saving that keeps us under $30k effective spend, that makes the internal case much easier.

I’ll pull finance contact info if you want to include them on the pricing doc.

— Ari

Ben / Marissa — forwarding the thread with FounderXYZ (Ari). Short ask: they are seed-stage, showing 27–30M tokens month-1 (ramp to ~120M/mo by month 6). Finance will greenlight up to $50k/mo without extra approvals. Ari asked for startup support that would effectively keep their cash outlay under ~$30k for the first 3 months if possible, plus committed-use pricing scenarios (3mo, 12mo) that progressively lower $/1M tokens.

Attached: founderxyz-token-profile.xlsx and my rough proposal draft (redwood-pricing-proposal-v2.pdf). Can you confirm what our standard allowed founder credit is for seed-stage (one free month? 50% off first month?), and whether we can layer that with a short-term committed discount for months 1–3? Also need guidance on minimums for a 12mo committed tier (is there a minimum committed token volume you want to require).

Ideally I’ll give them two concrete options:
A) Low-risk pilot: startup credit + consumption pricing with a small volume discount at the $/1M buckets.
B) Committed path: 12mo commit with stepped discounts that meet their long-term $/1M target if they ramp as forecasted.

Thanks — Chloe

Attachments: redwood-pricing-proposal-v2.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-20T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick recap & pricing ask — need guidance on allowable startup credit / committed bands

Chloe — quick note on what we can offer without needing VP sign-off:
- Startup program: one founder credit month equivalent to the estimated $/1M at the starter tier (i.e., credit covers first month up to 40M tokens).
- 3-month committed band (short-term commitment): we can offer a 10% off published unit rates when customers commit to an average of 30M tokens/month for 3 months. No minimum ARR requirement for this band.
- 12-month committed band: 20% off published unit rates if customer commits to an average of 70M tokens/month for 12 months. For ramping customers we allow a ramp schedule (month-by-month stated) but require an annualized minimum commitment of 50M tokens/month to qualify.

Pricing math (examples):
- Published base: $400 per 1M tokens (inference + base overhead)
- 3mo committed: $360 per 1M tokens (10% off) -> if they do 30M/mo, monthly spend = 30 * $360 = $10,800 (~$10.8k) — this doesn't align with their $40k–$60k page; note difference is likely because FounderXYZ’s token definition includes many system tokens; ensure alignment on how they count.
- 12mo committed (70M/mo @ 20% off): $320 per 1M -> monthly = 70 * $320 = $22,400.

Tiering note: if we layer a founder credit (one month free up to 40M), their first month effective cash outlay drops significantly which helps their sub-$30k target. The 12mo committed band gets them closer to the $300–$350 per 1M target if we apply additional multi-year rebate (we can discuss a 5% annual rebate for a 2-year extension).

Bottom line: give Ari two written options (pilot + founder credit OR 12mo commit at 20% with ramp schedule) and highlight how the first 3 months cash flows look side-by-side. I’ll approve the founder credit + 3mo commit structure; anything greater than 20% or longer-term rebates need Marissa OK for exec sign-off.

— Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: pricing model worksheet (internal)

Chloe — looks good. Ben’s guidance is aligned with policy. Approve the following go-to-customer language:

Option 1 — Pilot (recommended for FounderXYZ given early-stage budget):
- One founder credit month (covers up to 40M tokens).
- Consumption pricing at published rates for months 2–3 with a 10% short-term commit (3mo average) if they commit to 30M/month across the 3 months.
- No PO required if spend <= $50k/mo.

Option 2 — Growth commit (if they can lock 12mo):
- 12mo commit at an average of 70M tokens/month -> 20% off published rates.
- 2-year extension incentive: additional 5% rebate applied retroactively for year 2 if they meet the annualized commitment.

Chloe: proceed to send a short, plain-language proposal to Ari outlining both options and include a one-page table comparing cash flow months 1–6. Put the HubSpot deal link and attach the redwood-pricing-proposal-v2.pdf. If FounderXYZ verbally accepts, create a Docusign for the 3mo commit (Ben will fast-track).

— Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Strategy, Redwood Inference
